decisions.rationale: Familial adenomatous polyposis names one specific disease with a single definition and is used as a standalone disease mention (the subject of the opening sentence), not as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: FAP is the abbreviation of familial adenomatous polyposis. Abbreviations are annotated as a separate mention from the long form, and it refers to the same specific disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 6: Synonymous mentions (abbreviation definitions)

decisions.rationale: Colorectal cancer appears as a standalone disease mention (the object of predisposing to), not as an adjectival modifier. Cancer names are retained, and it is treated as a specific disease here.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease mentions; Annotation rule 5 (minimum necessary span)

decisions.rationale: FAP is used adjectivally to modify the noun 'patients' ('Dutch FAP patients'), so it is a disease mention serving as a modifier for another concept.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers

decisions.rationale: Familial adenomatous polyposis is the full long-form name of the specific disease, used as the subject of a clause ('familial adenomatous polyposis is caused by...') and not as a modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease mentions

decisions.rationale: FAP appears in the prepositional phrase 'among the FAP patients' and modifies the noun 'patients', so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 3: Disease mentions used as Modifiers

decisions.rationale: FAP is the object of 'presymptomatic diagnosis of FAP' and refers directly to the disease being diagnosed, so it is a standalone specific disease mention rather than an adjectival modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate 1: Specific Disease mentions
